properties.areaDesc: Gloucester, VA; Mathews, VA
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 22 at 12:14PM EDT until September 22 at 3:15PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
FFWAKQ

The National Weather Service in Wakefield has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Mathews County in eastern Virginia...
Central Gloucester County in southeastern Virginia...

* Until 315 PM EDT.

* At 1214 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Gloucester Courthouse, Hayes, Ark, Pinero, Belroi, Ware Neck,
Dutton, Fort Nonsense, Beulah, Selden, Soles, Pampa and
Allmondsville.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report flooding by calling 757-899-2415, posting to the NWS
Wakefield Facebook page, or using X @NWSWAKEFIELDVA.

properties.areaDesc: Southwest San Juan Mountains; San Juan River Basin
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 9:44AM MDT until September 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, San Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The ground remains saturated from recent heavy rainfall over the
past week. After a brief break, deep moisture is expected to
return to southwest Colorado Tuesday with a few inches of
rainfall possible during the Wednesday through Thursday
timeframe. In addition, multiple rounds of showers and
thunderstorms are expected Wednesday through Thursday evening
producing periods of heavy rainfall and potential flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Outer Banks; Hatteras Island
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 22 at 10:23AM EDT until September 22 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Watch, 2 to 3 feet of inundation above
ground level possible in low- lying areas near shorelines and
tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks and Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday afternoon
through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding may
extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and
businesses. Some roads and low lying property including parking
lots, parks, lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will
experience shallow flooding. Vulnerable areas along Highway 12
on Ocracoke and Hatteras Island are especially at risk for
inundation from the oceanside. Dangerous rip currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 10:00 AM today.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued September 22 at 10:23AM EDT until September 26 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Watch, 2 to 3 feet of inundation above
ground level possible in low- lying areas near shorelines and
tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks and Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday afternoon
through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding may
extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and
businesses. Some roads and low lying property including parking
lots, parks, lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will
experience shallow flooding. Vulnerable areas along Highway 12
on Ocracoke and Hatteras Island are especially at risk for
inundation from the oceanside. Dangerous rip currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 10:00 AM today.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 22 at 9:07AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:45 AM EDT Tuesday was 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady at flood stage.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM EDT.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets
and lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less

persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 22 at 6:28AM EDT until September 24 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, a high risk of rip
currents is expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to
one foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet expected
in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Watch, one to two feet
of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...The Maryland Beaches, Accomack, and Northampton County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this
morning through Wednesday evening. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 4 PM EDT Wednesday. For
the High Surf Advisory, from 2 AM Wednesday to 6 PM EDT
Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday
afternoon through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest
rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday
morning.

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared

* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents

shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 6 to 12 feet expected in the surf

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from 8 AM EDT this

Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 10 PM EDT this evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 8 PM this evening to 6 PM EDT
Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday afternoon
through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant beach erosion is likely
through this week and into the weekend. Moderate tidal
flooding could continue through Friday or perhaps longer.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop.

Be prepared to begin taking appropriate action to protect life
and property. Follow the recommendations of local emergency
management officials. Be sure to check the latest forecast from
time to time in case a warning is issued or any new information
becomes available.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 2:16AM MDT until September 24 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast New Mexico, including the following
areas, Central Lea, Eddy County Plains, Guadalupe Mountains of Eddy
County and Northern Lea and southwest Texas, including the
following areas, Eastern Culberson, Guadalupe Mountains Above 7000
Feet, Guadalupe and Delaware Mountains and Van Horn and Highway 54
Corridor.

* WHEN...From noon MDT  /1 PM CDT/ today through late Wednesday
night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A surge of deep tropical moisture and multiple upper level
disturbances will bring numerous to widespread showers and
thunderstorms capable of producing rounds of heavy rainfall that
may lead to flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 1:02AM MDT until September 23 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central,
northeast, southeast, and west central New Mexico, including the
following areas, in central New Mexico, Central Highlands, Eastern
Lincoln County, Estancia Valley, Lower Rio Grande Valley, Middle
Rio Grande Valley including the Albuquerque Metro Area, San Agustin
Plains and Adjacent Lowlands, Sandia and Manzano Mountains
including Edgewood, South Central Highlands, South Central
Mountains and Upper Tularosa Valley. In east central New Mexico, De
Baca County and Guadalupe County. In north central New Mexico, East
Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Espanola Valley, Glorieta Mesa
Including Glorieta Pass, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands,
Santa Fe Metro Area and Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains. In
northeast New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County, Far Northeast
Highlands, Harding County and Northeast Highlands. In southeast New
Mexico, Chaves County Plains and Southwest Chaves County. In west
central New Mexico, Southwest Mountains, West Central Highlands and
West Central Mountains.

* WHEN...From noon MDT today through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will arrive today and
Wednesday with widespread heavy rain.  Scattered occurrences of
flash flooding are likely, and there will probably be some main
stem river and tributary flooding, as the most likely rain amount
by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 1.5 inches many locations along
and east of the central mountain chain, and 1 inch in many
locations westward to around Dulce, Gallup, and Glenwood.
Stronger storms will produce torrential rainfall at rates over 2
inches per hour, and storms will train repeatedly in succession
over some locations, with locally heavier rain amounts reaching
over 4 inches over portions of southern, central, and eastern New
Mexico.  Heavy rain will likely continue Wednesday night over
north-central and eastern New Mexico, then showers and storms
with locally heavy rainfall are forecast to return to much of the
state again on Thursday.
- Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex
terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams.  As the event
unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone
to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of
storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 4:48PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern will continue across western Micronesia
with satellite imagery continuing to show areas of heavy showers and
thunderstorms. Latest satellite-dervied surface wind data depicts 15
to 20 mph west to southwest winds across western Yap State and Palau
with pockets of locally higher winds.

Weather models point to a continuation of these conditions with
periods of locally heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts, and choppy seas. Both
Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of Invest 91W, located near
13N142E, northeast of Yap. 91W is now the subject of a Tropical
Cyclone Formation Alert from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center and
showers are expected to remain mostly numerous to widespread and
heavy at times. Model guidance suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain per day
will be possible through Wednesday, especially for Yap.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next couple of days.
Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kings (Brooklyn), Southwest Suffolk, Southeast
Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...Today and again on Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Life-threatening rip currents are likely for all
people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting the beaches
should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The high rip current risk likely persists
through late week.
properties.instruction:

you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 4:12PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Conditions have generally tapered down across Majuro from yesterdays
wind and rain event. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms
will bring some locally heavy showers through tonight. Further north,
a tropical disturbance has produced robust convection across Bikini
Atoll and the far northern Marshall Islands today. This morning's
scatterometer shows that gusts could be approaching 40 to 45 knots in
the heaviest showers and thunderstorms. Some of this heavy weather
has made it as far south of Kwajalein today. Over the next couple of
days, model guidance shows a westward shift of the tropical
disturbance with a slow weakening trend. Scattered showers will
remain possible across the RMI this week with a monsoon-like pattern
remaining in place.

Seas could approach 9 to 12 feet where the strongest winds and
heaviest showers occur. This would make conditions hazardous to
Small Craft across the far northern RMI with extreme choppiness.
Boaters moving through the Marshall Islands north of Kwajalein
should practice enhanced caution over the next day or so.

For more information keep up to date with the latest information
from the Majuro Weather Service office and your local emergency
management agency.

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Delta Coast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 21 at 3:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
We are currently tracking a low that is expected to move through
the southern Bering Sea Thursday through Saturday and which could
approach the coast of the YK Delta. While the most likely storm
track south of our area would result in only modest rises in above
normal high water, a further north track could result in high
surf potential. As of right now, the southern portion of the YK
Delta coast could see water levels rise to around 1 to 3 feet
above the mean high water line. We will continue to monitor this
system closely.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF POTENTIAL FOR YUKON DELTA COAST TOWARD END OF THE WEEK

an Ozone Action Day for the Dallas-Fort Worth area for Tuesday,

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing

avoiding drive-through lanes, conserving energy, and keeping your
vehicle properly tuned.
